column1: #The mod's own windows for OpenHOI3 (script/openhoi/windows). Read by OpenHOI3 alone: the original does not open this folder.

column2: We hold $ENERGY$ energy, $CRUDE$ crude oil and $FUEL$ fuel.
Off: the game decides - it converts only while we hold more than twice as much energy as crude oil. On: the values below decide, within what our IC allows.
Energy to spend each day. More than our IC allows is cut to it.
Never take energy below this. What industry needs today is never converted whatever this says.
Convert only while we hold less crude oil than this. 0: no limit.
No energy can be turned into crude oil yet: technology puts the rate at $RATE$, and nothing converts at 0 or below.
Developing a synthetic industry opens it. What is set above applies from then.
Today: at most $CAP$ energy a day, each making $RATE$ crude oil. $FLOOR$ energy is kept for industry.
Off: the game decides - it refines until we hold more than a year of the crude oil coming in and more than twice our crude oil. On: the values below decide, within what our IC allows.
Crude oil to refine each day. More than our IC allows is cut to it.
Never take crude oil below this.
Refine only while we hold less fuel than this. 0: no limit. The game stops at 99,000 whatever this says.
Today: at most $CAP$ crude oil a day. How much fuel it makes is the game's: technology and laws.
All amounts are a day's, in stockpile units. Type the numbers and press Apply. A country nobody plays converts as the game decides.
The utility's data is not loaded: G_ImguiUtilityEnabled is off in script/utility_settings.lua.
Not researched. Showing level 1 for reference - it is not included in the stats above.
Copy the model string to the clipboard
Waiting for the game to apply this
Drag to choose, and let go to apply. Ctrl+click the slider to type a number instead. Investment converts base IC into IC days at the shown daily rate.
Whether the decision for setting a puppet's focus is offered in game. Turning it off hides the decision.
Select a puppet to set its focus.
No country has spare production of this resource.
A trade decision can be unavailable even when a country has resources spare: each trade applies a two day cooldown that blocks the buy decision while it is handled. Wait and watch your decisions.

The focus can be changed at any time, but the effects are not instant: a new focus takes about 90 days before it gives anything, and the old one wears off over as long as it was active for. Bonuses come in three tiers, reached after 90, 360 and 720 days.
Progress towards the next building each of your ministers will place. The counters are maintained by the AI, so nothing on this page can be set.
Reads the settings back from the game, discarding edits
Never configured - showing defaults. Apply to adopt them.
Applied, with values corrected to fit the limits
Edited - press Apply to send it to the game

How far into the red per day the AI may sell a resource. While a stockpile is above "Sell above", the AI sells that resource's daily balance plus this amount, drawing the stockpile down by up to this much a day. It cancels its sales once the daily balance falls below minus this amount.

Daily surplus is how much of a resource the AI keeps coming in each day beyond what the country actually needs. It only sells once the stockpile is above "Sell above", and cancels its own purchases once the stockpile is above "Stockpile". Supplies are left to the AI's own judgement.
Another category already uses this priority

This only takes effect with "Prioritize Upgrades/Custom" selected in the production window. IC is handed out in priority order, starting at 1, and each priority may only be used once. A category that cannot be paid for in full takes whatever is left and the ones after it get nothing. Anything still unspent goes to production. Amount is read either as a share of what the category needs or as a flat IC figure, depending on its mode.

Upgrades and reinforcement can be capped so an emergency cannot swallow the whole budget. Supply can be given a stockpile goal, which it puts a little extra IC towards until it is reached. Consumer goods can take 50% more IC while there is dissent.
The engine will not take more than $N$
Keeps producing officers for 10 more days, for a buffer of around 500

This only takes effect with "Slider AI" selected in the technology window. The numbers are resource amounts rather than slider positions: once a resource falls below its lower threshold the AI produces it until the upper threshold is reached, and how much leadership that takes is its own decision.

Officers cannot be set above 110, which is an engine limit. Diplomacy takes influences already running into account. Leadership is handed out to officers first, then spies, then diplomacy, and research takes whatever is left.
with the slider AI on, the game stops automatically continuing research once a level finishes.
No country selected - pages fall back to the actual player.
Any country's tag, whether anyone is playing it or not.
Press Get players to scan. In single player this lists only you.
A player can block the host from selecting their country. The selection silently stays put in that case.
Hiding a decision only takes it out of your own decision list. The AI carries on using it either way, so this is about a tidy list rather than about how the game plays.
Each run writes to its own folder, so a new game does not overwrite the last one. Assigned on the first collection.
Assigned when collection first writes something.
Meant for development: collection writes a file per statistic per country every day, which the game feels. Restricting it to a few countries keeps that in hand.
Every human player is collected while the switch above is off. The list is still editable.
Statistics appear here once collection has been switched on for a while. Each day writes one line per statistic.
Nothing to plot: the files ticked hold no readings.
The file carries on past a crash or a reload from an earlier save. Readings from the timeline that was abandoned are dropped rather than plotted alongside the one that replaced it.
Click it, then press the key to use. Escape cancels. A letter still types normally into a text box, so only a key pressed outside one opens the window.
Puts the window back where and as large as it first stood
Dark grey panels with a blue accent. Easiest to pick out over a busy map.
Paper: the window as a document over the map. For playing in daylight, or if the dark style is hard to read.
Dark blue panels, the drawing library's first look.
Scrolling the map at the screen edge, where event popups appear and the two custom autosaves are in the game's own Options window on OpenHOI3, on its Game tab.
Reads the mod's modifier files, which takes a moment.
What each national focus gives once it has been active long enough. A tier includes everything from the tiers before it only where the mod repeats it, so read each column on its own.
Base values only. These modifiers are local - national and global ones are not included here.
Select a unit on the left.
Puts this unit's details, and its regiments, on the clipboard as text
Nothing - this is the bottom of the tree.
Puts the whole report on the clipboard as text
Counts below a formation exclude the formation itself, so a theatre's land count is the units under its command rather than a count that includes it.
This country has no regiments of that branch.
Dates as the game counts them: year.month.day, the way they are written in the list below. Both ends are included, the last one for the whole of its day.
Back to 31 days ending today - the range the page starts at. Whatever is typed in the two boxes is replaced.
not a date - write it as 1936.1.1 | showing $FROM$ to $TO$

Every battle is added as it finishes and kept with the savegame. Loading an earlier save brings back the record as it stood then. The Total column adds unlike things: a naval battle's losses are ships, a raid's are of another kind again.
Nothing recorded for $TAG$ yet. Battles are added as they finish.
Click for the figures of the entire unit.
No province has any of this.
Each shade starts at the amount under it. $COUNT$ provinces have any. The scale runs from the 1% with the least to the 1% with the most, so everything above $TOP$ shares the top shade.
Levels 1 to 10, the same ladder the infrastructure map climbs.
Grey: none here - light where you can see the province, dark where not.
Grey: nothing to show. Only provinces you have the intel for - your own and your allies' - show any supply. The rest are dark grey.
§GRight click§W for what else this map mode can show.

How many days the supplies in the province last its units, at what they use a day. Each shade starts at the number of days under it. The game keeps a province stocked for 35 days of its need, so a well supplied one sits in the top shade. Only provinces with units that use supplies are shaded.

How many days the fuel in the province lasts its units, at what they use a day. Each shade starts at the number of days under it. The game keeps a province stocked for 35 days of its need, so a well supplied one sits in the top shade. Only provinces with units that use fuel are shaded.

How far the province is from the depot that supplies it. Supply is handed along province by province, so the further it has to travel, the less of it arrives. Poor infrastructure makes a province count as two or three instead of one, so a route across bad ground is further than it looks on the map. Each shade starts at the number under it. Depots themselves are the top shade, provinces with no supply line at all the bottom one, and land in no supply network is grey.

How much of that distance is poor infrastructure rather than real distance. Zero means the way to the depot is good all the way and costs nothing extra. Eight means the route counts as eight provinces longer than it really is, because of what it crosses. This is the number that building infrastructure brings down. Provinces with no supply line at all show nothing.

How much of what the province can pass on in a day is asked of it today - its own units' shortfall and what provinces further out want through it. Each shade starts at the share under it. At 100% the line through here is full, and anything beyond waits. How much a province can pass on is the game's own figure, worked out from the province's modifiers and its controller's.
The same for fuel, which shares the province's capacity figure: how much of what it can pass on in a day is asked of it today. At 100% the line through here is full.

What a load of supplies or fuel loses crossing the province - the same amount whatever the size of the load, so a long line of small loads loses the most. Half on the controller's own ground, more in mud unless the ground is frozen, more again where partisans are active in occupied land, less with the controller's supply technologies. Each shade starts at the tax under it. Land in no supply network is grey.
Supplies passed on through the province today, on their way out from the depot - the supply lines themselves.
Fuel passed on through the province today, on its way out from the depot.
Supplies in the province. A capital's are the country's whole stockpile, so it sits in the top shade.
Fuel in the province. A capital's is the country's whole stockpile, so it sits in the top shade.
This game does not collect statistics: the rule was turned off in the lobby.
Writes every country's every statistic as a file, in the layout the plotting tool reads

§YGame statistics, kept in your savegame.§W
Every day the game notes each country's figures, so that you can plot them later on the utility's Statistics page:
 - leadership and how it is shared out
 - spies and neutrality
 - IC, its efficiency and the production sliders
 - the popularity of each ideology
 - provinces owned and controlled, units and manpower
 - stockpiles, daily balance and trade of each resource

§GNothing about you or your computer is collected, and nothing is sent anywhere.§W
The record is part of the savegame and adds about half a megabyte to it for each year played. Turn this off to keep saves smaller.
Draws every series into the same axes instead of one plot each

§YLets a player in whose OpenHOI3 checksum does not match the host's.§W
The checksum as calculated by the original game still has to match, but it does not cover all of the game files.

§RIf the mismatched files cause the players' simulations to differ, the game will be resynced each midnight.§W

§YRecords the game, so that it can be played back later.§W\nThe recording is kept beside your savegames, and every save remembers its place in the timeline. A game can be played back from its start up to the selected save. You can also create a new save during the replay and continue playing from there.\n - In multiplayer only the host records the game, and only the host can watch the replay.

§YPlays back the game that led to this save.§W
The game runs again from its start, through every save and load made on the way, up to this save. You only look on: nothing you press changes the game. Pause and speed work as usual.
 - Select a country on the map first to watch the game through its eyes. With none selected you watch the country that played.
It is made of $COUNT$ recordings, and the game is loaded once for each.

§RThis replay was recorded with another engine version or other rules.§W
 - recorded with: $MADE$
 - this engine: $NOW$
You can watch it, but it may not play back as it was played. Where the game goes another way, the replay stops.
The replay no longer fits this engine and stops here
Replay: the game was saved and loaded here...
§YLook on through another country.§W\nShows that country's screens, its units and what it knows of the map. Countries marked with * were played by a person. The game being played back is not changed.

§YWrites this save and its replay as one file.§W
The file can be given to another player, who imports it with Import replay. It is written to:
$FOLDER$
It only plays back with the same engine version and the same game files.

§YTakes in replay files from another player.§W
Put the files into:
$FOLDER$
Each one's save is then added to your saved games, where you can load it and watch its replay. Files waiting: $COUNT$
Replay imported: $FILE$ is now among your saved games
$FILE$ is not a replay file and was left where it is
Load a saved game that was recorded to use this.
Timing runs from the first time this page is opened until Stop, also while it is closed.
Timing is switched off. Start switches it on again.
Measured for $SECONDS$ seconds: $HOURS$ game hours, $DAYS$ of them turning a day.
No hour has run yet. Unpause the game.
Speed now: $HOURS$ game hours a second, which is $DAYS$ game days a minute.
An hour that turns a day
The steps of the game's hours

A step is named as the engine names it. Click a heading to sort by it, and again to turn the order round. An indented line is a part of the step above it and is counted in that step as well. Parts that run side by side on several processor threads can add up to more than their step.
This game is played by the original's rules. It has no fixes to switch.

Every fix of the enhanced engine, switched on or off for the game being played. A change holds at once, also while the game is paused, and is saved with the game. A figure made once a day or once a month follows at its next making. A new game starts with what common/openhoi_enhanced.txt says.
Only the host may switch a fix.
Acts as the files are read. Set it in common/openhoi_enhanced.txt and restart.

column1: #A fix's description on that page: OPENHOI_FIX_ and the fix's name in capitals.

column2: A minister's technology decay modifier counts. The original throws it away.
The Simplified Terrain map mode colours the sea by its terrain, as it does the land.
A country-level ic modifier counts as off-map IC. The original never reads it.

Screens the original writes once and then leaves are kept up to date: the province view, the technology panel, a diplomacy row, the list of trades, a fleet's cargo, the air map mode's colours and the list of decisions. Display only.
Closing the in-game menu starts the clock again where the menu stopped it, also after Save Game, Game Options or Message Settings was opened.
A tooltip is kept from leaving the screen at the left and the top too. Display only.

Figures the original shows wrongly are shown as they are: a fleet's positioning penalty, a production slider with nothing needed, a fleet's organisation regain at sea, tribute as a loss, a leader's experience at skill 11 and the ground's attrition in the division designer. Display only.
A new unit's number takes the ending of its last two digits: 111th, 112th, 113th, where the original writes 111st, 112nd, 113rd. Changes the names of units made from then on.
With several air units selected, the orders window greys a mission that any of them may not fly. The original offers the first unit's missions and hands them to all.
In a province's history and a unit file, a key with no equals sign takes the word after it. The original gives the key the value of the pair before it.
A unit figure of more than three decimals is cut to three: 0.3375 is 0.337, where the original reads 3.375.
A province's yield of fuel is scaled by global_fuel and of money by global_money. The original has the two the wrong way round.
A technology's repair_cost_multiplier for a unit type is added with its other figures. The original leaves it out of the sum.
A leader's dissent_impact scales what dissent costs his unit at sea, in the air and under bombs, as it does on land.
A raid on a convoy counts the hours the raider's leader banked in it towards his traits, so seawolf can be earned by raiding.
A unit defending behind a whole level of fort has its leaders' fort_defence on its attack and defence. The original reaches the trait only for an attacker, where it does nothing.
A radar station's reach is longer by its country's radar_efficiency.
The side that picks its combat tactic second rolls its leader's surprise_chance, and under it takes the tactic that counters the other side's. One roll more for a side with the trait.
A historical model that asks for a level above the one held loses to every model that does not, so a country is not shown a model it has not researched. Display only.
A queued brigade's historical model gives a level for every technology of its type, so no level lands on the technology before it.
A finished building waiting to be placed may go where its country has not researched it. Ordering one still asks for the technology.
A land leader a file of units puts on a land unit of his own country takes the rank of that unit's level and is put in service.
A leader put in service on the day his history first gives him a rank takes the rank that line names, where the original gives rank 1.
A save keeps each country's candidate events, so a loaded game fires events from its first day. The original's fires none until its month turns.
With Ctrl held, agreeing to the leader window's remove all leaders takes the leaders off the selected units alone.
A tooltip taller than the screen shows as many lines as fit and is moved through with Alt and the wheel, or Alt and the Up or Down key.
The AI joins a small air group to another only where its own splitting rule would not take a wing out again. The original joins and splits the mod's own air types for the whole game.
A payment on a debt comes off the debt, so it is paid off after YEARS_TO_REPAY_DEBT years of peace. The original never lowers a debt.
Revoking a country's leave to run a debt costs the creditor who revokes. The original charges the debtor.
A lend-lease receiver whose share is more than the giver's stockpile pays for is given what it does pay for. The original gives it nothing.
Each side of a land battle picks its tactic by its own leader's aggressiveness. The original's attacker picks by the defender's leader and its defender by none.
A ship that fires on its own side fires on the ship its roll points to. The original's always ends on the last ship of the last fleet.
has_combined_arms = no in a tactic's or a trait's trigger holds where no unit has combined arms. The original reads nothing after the key.
A strategic redeployment draws its attack delay once, on arrival, and holds it at its base on the way. The original draws a new one every hour.
Interdiction flies at the province of its list where the most of the enemy is on the move, and with no enemy in any of them at one by a draw. The original takes the last it sees.
An air unit raiding convoys waits at its base until its next try is due. The original's flies out at once and wastes every other sortie.
offmap_political_intel and peace_offmap_intel, which the original reads nowhere, add to how well the country knows another. 0.1 is worth one spy.
The next song is drawn by its chance. The original always takes the heaviest.
The order that sets an occupation policy asks the policy's allow as the button does, and a policy goes back to none once the two are at peace.
A ship type's extra_amphibious_defence counts for the brigades it names, and a landing with no invasion defence has the define's penalty exactly.
The south of the map has seasons, the north's half a year on, with the cold and the days of its latitude. The original's south is summer all year. Moves the balance.
A wing's air_defence meets shots in an air battle, as a unit's defence does on land. The original works it out and never reads it. Moves the balance.
A message's text on the map lives by the second, not by the frame. Display only.
